moved.sentence: `remember(keys) { expensive() }` to cache costly computation across recompositions; recompute only when a key changes.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: use remember(keys) to cache costly computation across recompositions, recomputing only when a key changes, with the keyed-derived-results example.

moved.sentence: Do **NOT** perform backwards writes — never write to a state value that the same composable already read; this loops recomposition.

judged.note: The unkeyed 'Do NOT' is kept and strengthened to MUST NOT, with the never-write-to-already-read-state definition and the recomposition-loop reason.

moved.sentence: Keep composables side-effect free and idempotent.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: composables side-effect free and idempotent.

moved.sentence: Avoid allocating new collections, lambdas-with-captures, or objects in the composable body on every call; hoist or `remember` them.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with all three allocation kinds, the every-call scope and the hoist-or-remember remedy.
Kept at SHOULD: read state as late as possible.

moved.sentence: Hoist the read into a lambda-based modifier so a value change triggers only layout/draw, not recomposition: `Modifier.offset { IntOffset(x, y) }`, `Modifier.graphicsLayer { alpha = a }`, `Modifier.drawBehind { ... }`.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the layout/draw-not-recomposition reason and all three lambda-modifier examples.

moved.sentence: Pass **lambdas** instead of already-read values when the value changes frequently (e.g. scroll/animation): `Counter(count = { viewModel.count })` defers the read to the consumer.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the frequently-changing condition, the scroll/animation example and the deferred-read Counter example.

moved.sentence: Use `derivedStateOf { ... }` when a frequently-changing state should drive UI only when a **computed** result crosses a threshold (e.g.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the computed-threshold condition and the firstVisibleItemIndex > 0 example.

moved.sentence: Do not use it for one-to-one transforms — that adds overhead with no benefit.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD NOT with the referent made explicit (derivedStateOf) and the overhead-with-no-benefit reason.

moved.sentence: Profile **release** builds with R8 enabled and a **Baseline Profile** applied.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with both conditions: R8 enabled and a Baseline Profile applied.

moved.sentence: Debug builds run unoptimized Compose and produce misleading numbers — never tune against them.

judged.note: The misleading-debug-numbers reason is kept and 'never tune against them' is strengthened to MUST NOT.

moved.sentence: Use **Layout Inspector** recomposition counts to find composables recomposing more than expected; a high count signals an unstable parameter or an un-deferred read.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the find-over-recomposing-composables purpose and the unstable-parameter / un-deferred-read diagnosis.

moved.sentence: For regression gates, use Macrobenchmark (frame timing, `recompositionCount`) on representative journeys.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD for regression gates, with frame timing, recompositionCount and representative journeys.

moved.sentence: Optimize a hotspot **only** after a measurement justifies it (per make-it-work-make-it-right-make-it-fast); do not pre-optimize composables that are not hot.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD / SHOULD NOT: optimize only after measurement justifies it (with the principle reference) and do not pre-optimize composables that are not hot.
Kept at SHOULD: composables are passed immutable data.

moved.sentence: Prefer `val` over `var`, `kotlinx.collections.immutable` (`ImmutableList`/`PersistentList`) over `List`, and data classes whose properties are themselves stable.

judged.note: All three preferences (val over var, kotlinx immutable collections over List, data classes with stable properties) are kept at SHOULD.
Kept at SHOULD, with the strong-skipping-does-not-make-a-type-stable context that motivates it.

moved.sentence: Annotate `@Immutable` (deeply unchanging) or `@Stable` (changes only via `State`) **only** when the type is truly so and the compiler cannot infer it (e.g., a type from a module without the Compose compiler, or one using an interface field).

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the only-when-truly-so-and-compiler-cannot-infer condition, the definitions of @Immutable/@Stable and both examples.

moved.sentence: A false annotation causes missed recompositions and stale UI — do not annotate to silence the compiler.

judged.note: The missed-recompositions/stale-UI reason is kept and 'do not annotate to silence the compiler' is kept at SHOULD NOT.
